assessments.scope: Preview influence reduction and earlier collider ordering
assessments.assessment: The preview chooses four individual influence slots; the shared rig/export reducer combines equal joint ordinals before choosing four. A symbolic positive duplicate-ordinal row can select different four-slot representations. Separately, collider deformation precedes the weighted cloth target joint-count check. A supported duplicate or mismatched asset, required equivalence, panic or rendered effect has not been established.
assessments.history: The e275 059 named preview-layout suspicion was source-qualified and rejected only in its stated scope. All 13 cited original records were recovered; eight named e275/current source files match individually. Their bytes do not establish whole-tree equality or transfer reader credit. q167, q175, q436 and q572 remain separately attributed related contracts.

assessments.scope: Hair/body Arc identity, cached model dependency and worker lifecycle
assessments.assessment: The hair match compares groom and body Arc identity, so a different equal-count Arc does not match. A same-LOD corrective reload may instead reuse the same earlier body Arc through a cache key that omits model/corrective identity; this is connected to the already recorded cache policy, with actual model output and assets open. Replacing an unfinished worker handle leaves the old worker to finish and does not install its result through that discarded handle. Reconstructed BodyHead work can also precede an in-progress match; timing, resource cost and intended policy are unproved.
assessments.history: The e275 historical record rejected a simple equal-count stale-body suspicion only in its named scope. The q2327 cache disposition and q2323 fit/model relationship are separate historical/current records; retain their reviewers, original revision and open policy.

assessments.scope: Cancelled drape jobs, request/tag pairing and restart checkpoints
assessments.assessment: The active request holds tag/input pairs together, suppresses cancelled progress, and creates fresh cancellation/preview objects for replacement work, supporting only the historical named-scope stale-tag rejection. Separately, a fresh restart clears stored checkpoints before polling can take checkpoints from an active cancelled outcome and pass them to a pending request. An eligible reusable old stage, supported sequence, impact and intended restart policy remain unproved.
assessments.history: The e275 059 rejection remains source-qualified only for its named tag-association scope, not its parent or a global closure. The original packet contains local paths and is separately held; its publicly scanned successor reconstructs five path-containing files and preserves the other original members byte-for-byte.

assessments.scope: Inventory diagnostics, graph error precedence and review output
assessments.assessment: Three conditional first operations are distinct: wear drops the fit culprit ID and the UI explains using the requested ID; the creator graph adapter can prefer a recomputed occupied reason over a core reason; and recipe review writes body.json before resolving all worn items. A different invalid worn item, a fully specified accepted conflicting catalog/recipe, actual partial output, severity and desired diagnostic/atomicity policies remain open. The separately inspected core catalog occupancy validator rejects its conflicting example when actually applied; the shown creator loader does not invoke that separate validator.
assessments.history: The 059 e275 error-boundary record is a documented conditional policy question with discovery closed only within its named historical scope. Seventeen cited originals matched and six named files match e275/95e individually. q2330 successor arithmetic and broad catalog/equipment records are related but distinct.

assessments.scope: Inventory ID successor arithmetic and selected native deserialization source
assessments.assessment: Inventory::add computes each existing ID plus one before taking the maximum. For distinct symbolic IDs u64::MAX-1 and u64::MAX, checked arithmetic would panic before insertion; wrapping arithmetic could select the already occupied maximum. Structural recipe checks do not bound IDs and selected locked serde source supports parsing the maximum u64 without parser execution. An actual accepted recipe, effective overflow profile, initialization and effect remain unobserved. This is additional evidence for existing REVIEW-CREATOR-INVENTORY-ID-SUCCESSOR-001, not a new unique count.

The frozen 6533, e275 and 95e inventory objects match individually; the dirty frozen working tree is not established clean. PL13-113, PL13-116 and the e275 reader/adoption keep distinct attribution. The public successor omits two exact upstream archives containing author/contact patterns; locked selected source files and identity crosswalk are retained, while the full original packet remains separately held.
